findings.title: canManage() returns true for admins holding only the 'view' scope on the Groups resource type
findings.body: In the no-arg canManage(), the fallback calls hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE), so a delegated admin who was granted a scope permission with only the 'view' scope on the all-groups resource passes this check. canManage()/requireManage() is what guards group creation in GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup (POST /admin/realms/{realm}/groups), so a view-only groups admin can create top-level groups. The sibling method canManage(GroupModel) correctly checks only the MANAGE scope. The new tests never assert that a view-only grantee is forbidden from creating groups. Remove VIEW from the scope list in canManage() (the GroupPermissionEvaluator javadoc for canManage() mirrors the same wrong VIEW-or-MANAGE text and should be corrected too).

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() evaluates and returns Resource.getId() instead of the group id (resource name)
findings.body: In the V2 schema, per-group authorization resources are stored with the group id as the resource *name* (AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource -> resolveGroup returns group.getId()). The callback passes groupResource.getId() (the Resource entity UUID) to hasPermission, which looks it up with resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId) — that never matches, so evaluation silently falls back to the all-groups resource instead of each group's own resource, and per-group view-members/manage-members permissions are never detected. It then adds groupResource.getId() (again the wrong UUID) into the granted set; callers put this set into the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute (UsersResource.searchForUser, BruteForceUsersResource) and into getUsersCount, which filter by group ids. Consequences: (a) for per-group grants the DB-level group restriction is never applied, so user searches run unfiltered with pagination applied before the canView post-filter (wrong pages, wrong counts); (b) when an admin has view-members on ALL groups, the all-groups resource (name 'Groups', not a group id) matches the iteration and its resource UUID is added as a bogus group id, so user search returns nothing and count returns 0 for an admin who should see everyone. Use groupResource.getName() in both the hasPermission call and granted.add, and skip the resource whose name equals the type name.

findings.title: Per-group resources created by getOrCreateResource have no type set, so findByType("Groups") never returns them
findings.body: getOrCreateResource creates the per-group resource via resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId()) and updates its scopes, but never calls setType (compare V1 GroupPermissions.initialize, which explicitly calls groupResource.setType("Group")). GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission enumerates group resources with resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...); since resources created here have a null type, they are never enumerated — only the 'Groups' all-resource (whose type is set in init()) matches. Even after fixing the id/name confusion in getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, per-group view permissions would still be invisible to it. The same gap exists for per-user/per-client resources created through this method, but it only becomes observable with the new Groups findByType usage.

findings.title: Group removal event now hits UnsupportedOperationException in V2, breaking group deletion or leaking orphaned authorization data
findings.body: AdminPermissions.registerListener handles GroupModel.GroupRemovedEvent by calling management(session, realm).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false) whenever the admin-fine-grained-authz (v1) feature is enabled. Before this PR, MgmtPermissionsV2 inherited groups() from MgmtPermissions and returned the v1 GroupPermissions, whose setPermissionsEnabled was a harmless no-op against a v2 realm; now MgmtPermissionsV2.groups() returns GroupPermissionsV2, whose setPermissionsEnabled unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException. As a result, deleting any group fails with a server error (the exception propagates out of realm.removeGroup) when both admin-fine-grained-authz and admin-fine-grained-authz-v2 are enabled. Conversely, with only v2 enabled the listener is not registered at all (registration is gated on the v1 feature), so a deleted group's authorization resource and all scope permissions referencing it are left orphaned in the store. V2 needs a real cleanup implementation for group removal (and the v1-only management/permissions endpoint should degrade gracefully instead of throwing).

findings.title: No migration path: realms that already enabled admin permissions never get the 'Groups' resource and the three new scopes
findings.body: The 'Groups' resource-type resource and the manage-membership/manage-members/view-members scopes are only created in AdminPermissionsSchema.init(), which returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() != null. Realms that enabled admin permissions (FGAP v2 preview) before this change keep their existing admin-permissions client untouched, so the new schema objects are never created. Consequences: (a) creating a group permission fails in getOrCreateResource, where scope lookup by name misses and throws ModelException("No scopes found."); (b) GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission's fallback calls AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...), which returns null when the 'Groups' resource is absent, and then calls policyStore.findByResource(server, null), producing a server error on group admin endpoints for delegated admins. An update mechanism is needed that syncs schema scopes and resource-type resources for pre-existing admin-permissions clients.

findings.title: getResourceName() has no handling for the Groups resource type
findings.body: getResourceName is the mechanism that translates per-object authorization resources into human-readable names for display (for Users it returns "All users" for the type resource and the username otherwise). For Groups resources — whose resource name is the group's UUID — it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(), which is null for resources created via getOrCreateResource, so group permissions will be displayed with a blank or raw UUID identifier in the admin console. It should resolve the group analogously to the Users branch ("All groups" for the type resource, group name otherwise).

findings.title: Javadoc for requireManageMembers references the wrong check method
findings.body: The newly added javadoc for requireManageMembers(GroupModel) says "Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canManageMembership(GroupModel)} returns false" — it should reference canManageMembers(GroupModel). Additionally, the javadoc for getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() says "@return Stream of IDs of groups with view permission" although the method returns a Set. Since these docs describe authorization checks, the wrong references are misleading to implementers.
